transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-07-09 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Narayanan (Redwood SE), Ethan Cho (SummitAI Security Lead), Marisol Reyes (Platform Eng), Liam O'Neill (Product), Anika Patel (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto):
SummitAI pilot weekly sync focused on security gating items: SSO/SAML specifics, audit log format and retention policy, SOC2 evidence request, and next pilot benchmark. Agreement to exchange SOC2 artefacts, audit log schema, and to finalize retention SLAs. Action items assigned.

Topics: SSO integration details; audit logs and retention; SOC2 evidence; data residency concerns; next benchmark run.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off — this is the weekly pilot sync for SummitAI, focused on the security gates. thanks for the time.
[00:08] Ethan: thanks Jordan, appreciate it. quick note I've got to step out around 16:05 UTC but i'll stay for the core SSO bit.
[00:13] Jordan: perfect. priya, want to take the tech pass on SSO?
[00:16] Priya: yeah sure — so last week we got the SAML metadata from summit, thanks marisol. i did a dry run of the IdP assertion mapping, couple of fields we need to align: the groups claim is coming back as "roles" and not "groups", and the email_verified flag is missing so we need to map on email principal. also noted the NameID format is transient, not persistent, so we recommended persistent.
[00:40] Marisol: yah our IdP team uses a short-lived name id for privacy reasons, we can flip it if it's required. question — does Redwood require persistent to keep the session mapping for the KV cache?
[00:50] Priya: not strictly; we can cookie map to the session but for audit and RBAC you want a stable principal. there was also a small mismatch on the attribute namespace — i sent a screenshot to marisol after the call last week.
[01:04] Liam: sorry can i ask a dumb question — if we change to persistent NameID, what is the timeline? will it break other internal integrations?
[01:10] Marisol: somewhat, we have to coordinate with internal apps, maybe a 2 week window with dev time.
[01:15] Ethan: that's okay, we can plan for a canary. the security gate wants to see SSO mapped and provisioning working before we move to dedicated capacity.
[01:22] Jordan: makes sense. for the pilot we'll accept the temporary mapping as long as the audit logs clearly show principal identifiers. speaking of audit logs — priya, can you walk through the events we emit?
[01:32] Priya: sure. we emit an event per request: timestamp, request_id, model_id, user_principal, route, token_usage, latency_ms, decisioning route, and optional kv_hit boolean. also we emit session start/end and auth events. i do want to call out that some of the field names in today's export are a bit abbreviated — e.g., "kv" became "k-v" in auto tooling, so the schema might show k dash v.
[02:00] Marisol: ha, that will make our parsers sad. can you put a canonical schema in a doc?
[02:05] Priya: yes, i'm preparing that now — i'll include JSON schema and an example event with pii redacted.
[02:12] Jordan: great. Ethan, what retention window is security expecting for logs?
[02:16] Ethan: for pilot we asked for 90 days, for prod it's 7 years for compliance reasons. but we can start pilot at 90 as long as we have a path to extend.
[02:26] Anika: quick legal note — if you have legal hold requests we need the ability to export data in a forensically sound format. also encryption at rest and key management are checkboxes for us.
[02:36] Jordan: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private. For hosted pilot we can provide provider-managed encryption but we also have an offer for bring-your-own-key on Dedicated.
[02:48] Anika: ok please include that nuance in the DPA.
[02:53] Jordan: will do.
[02:55] [02:55] Priya: one more on audit — we also produce a separate system audit stream with change events for model rollouts, config changes, and policy switches. those are separate from request telemetry. they have admin actor, before/after, and timestamp.
[03:12] Liam: perfect, that's actually super helpful. can you show an example of the rollout change event?
[03:17] Priya: yep, example in the doc: { actor: "redwood:deploy-bot", target: "model:openlm-v2", change: "rollout 10->30%", ts: ... } (note: transcript may have formatting issues)
[03:33] Ethan: on SOC2 — we requested the scope and the latest attestation; Jordan you said you'd share those?
[03:38] Jordan: yes i have the SOC 2 type II summary and the auditor letter — i'll send the redacted PDF after this call. if you need the full bridge letter we can coordinate NDA with our compliance team.
[03:49] Ethan: that's good. we also want to validate controls for privileged access and separation of duties. how does Redwood handle admin access across Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:58] Jordan: on Hosted our SRE/Platform teams have least privilege and actions are audited. on Dedicated we offer customer-only access groups and can restrict Redwood ops. We have RBAC and can lock down runtime control plane.
[04:12] Priya: and all admin actions are logged to the system audit stream i mentioned.
[04:17] Marisol: good. question about data residency — some of our EU customers require logs to stay in eu-west. can we scope retention per region?
[04:26] Jordan: yes, we can pin storage region for logs in both Hosted and Dedicated. for pilot we'll keep eu logs in eu-west as requested.
[04:33] Anika: also curious about eDiscovery — how quickly can you produce a set of events if legal demands them?
[04:41] Priya: typical turnaround for a scoped export is 72 hours for hosted; with dedicated or private deployments we can do same-day exports depending on support SLAs.
[04:51] Liam: okay that aligns with our expectations.
[04:55] [05:00] Jordan: switching to retention and deletion — if a user requests deletion, how does Redwood handle removing data from logs that contain the user principal?
[05:07] Priya: we redact PII in the audit stream on request and issue a tombstone for the identifier; underlying raw logs in archived buckets are retained per retention policy for forensic reasons but access is gated and encrypted. for private deployments customers typically manage the deletion lifecycle themselves.
[05:25] Ethan: can you put that in the security page? we need clear language for our SecOps runbook.
[05:30] Jordan: yep i'll add that.
[05:33] Marisol: about SSO provisioning — we want SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle. is that in scope for this pilot?
[05:39] Priya: SCIM is supported on Dedicated — for hosted pilot we can do manual provisioning or delegated SAML + just-in-time provisioning in the IdP. full SCIM is on roadmap and can be prioritized if you commit to Dedicated.
[05:52] Ethan: just-in-time is fine for pilot. for production we'll need SCIM.
[05:56] Jordan: noted. we'll include an options matrix in the follow-up.
[06:01] [06:10] Priya: quick performance note: we ran a run last night against your sample traffic — 95th latency was about 320ms on default batching, after we tuned request multiplexing it dropped to 210ms. if you push model sequence length up we see higher p95.
[06:25] Marisol: where can we see the raw benchmark?
[06:27] Priya: link in the pilot folder — i'll post it again, also the CSV has per-route breakdown.
[06:33] Jordan: for the governance gate we want two things: (1) SSO mapped and audit logs flowing to your intake, (2) a SOC2 attestation in the folder. once those are in place we can run the dedicated-capacity smoke test.
[06:45] Ethan: that's the bar. anything else?
[06:48] Anika: legal will need DPA edits, i'll surface comments in the doc.
[06:52] Jordan: ok, recap of action items — i'll send SOC2/artifacts, priya will upload audit schema sample, ethan to confirm retention window, anika to review DPA. any blockers?
[07:03] Liam: timeline concern on persistent NameID but we can live with JIT for pilot.
[07:08] Jordan: good. next sync — want to do the benchmark overlay next Wednesday at same time?
[07:12] Ethan: yes, let's do that.
[07:15] Marisol: can we also have a short 15-minute session with your SRE to go over export mechanics?
[07:20] Jordan: sure, i'll schedule a follow-up with our SRE, call it "export mechanics deep-dive".
[07:25] [07:25] Priya: i'll include the sample event payload and JSON schema in the pilot folder after this. note — some names may get garbled by automated tooling so double-check keys like kv_hit vs k_v_hit.
[07:36] Ethan: thanks everyone. i'll follow up on the retention question and loop in infra.
[07:40] Jordan: thanks all, we'll send the docs shortly.
